title: Invincible
synopsis: You're the strongest person on Earth this week. The Viltrumites are watching, your father is back in your inbox, and you have an econ midterm at 9 a.m. Try not to bleed on the textbook.

nodes.text: Your phone explodes — a literal explosion, in the next county; figuratively, your phone — and your professor reminds you the midterm is at nine. You're wearing flannel pants and have a black eye from yesterday.

choices.text: Take the call and skip the test
Try to do both somehow
choices.consequence: Optimism is a kind of strategy.

nodes.text: It's a familiar villain — Titan, who hates his name — robbing a federal vault for what he insists are honest reasons. A man yells at him about labor rights. The vault yells back electronically.

choices.text: Knock Titan out fast and clean
Talk to Titan first

nodes.text: You're a hundred feet up reading econ notes off your phone. A pigeon hits you in the face. The notes get worse from here.

choices.text: Fly to campus first
choices.consequence: Take the test, then save the city.

choices.text: Tutor yourself by saving someone who knows econ
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Multi-task heroically—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Your girlfriend Eve is on the line, in her own crisis — a refugee camp under threat from a warlord whose helicopters her energy fields can't politely stop forever. She wants backup, not advice.

choices.text: Promise her you'll be there in twenty minutes
Send the Guardians instead

nodes.text: Mom: 'Dinner Sunday. Please. Your sister is asking. PS your Dad emailed me again.' The Dad in question is Nolan, who once tried to kill you, who lives, when he lives, off-planet.

choices.text: Reply 'I'll be there'
Delete the email-about-Dad screenshot before reading

nodes.text: You arrive with Eve as four helicopters lift off. She is exhausted and brilliant. The warlord is shouting demands; the camp's elder is, somehow, also shouting demands at the warlord. You have ninety seconds.

choices.text: Disable the helicopters non-lethally
Take the warlord directly and remove him
choices.consequence: Solve the problem, not the helicopters.

nodes.text: Robot, ever-tense, calls back. Two of the Guardians are out on Mars-related business. The team is thin. He suggests you 'prioritize ruthlessly.' He always says that. You always hate it.

choices.text: Send Robot to Eve, you take the vault
choices.consequence: Trade routes that fit each strength.

choices.text: Send Robot to the vault, you take Eve

nodes.text: Cecil from the GDA grabs your comm. 'Viltrumite ship just blinked into orbit,' he says. 'It hasn't done anything yet.' He pauses, in the way Cecil pauses. 'Mark, your father may be on it.'

choices.text: Fly to orbit immediately
Stay grounded until you know more
choices.consequence: Don't pop the bubble until you have to.

nodes.text: Your ex Amber appears outside the lecture hall with two coffees and a small kind smile. 'I heard about Tuesday,' she says. 'I just wanted to make sure you're still here.' It's the kindest sentence anyone has said this week.

choices.text: Take the coffee and be honest about everything
Smile, thank her, and keep moving

nodes.text: The Viltrumite ship hangs over Earth like a quiet threat. The hatch opens. It is not your father. It is Lucan, a Viltrumite governor with the smile of a person who has never been told no on a planetary scale.

choices.text: Pretend to negotiate
choices.consequence: “Pretend to negotiate” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Buy minutes.

choices.text: Hit him first

nodes.text: You make it to Sunday dinner late, bruised, in time for dessert. Your little sister hugs your leg and refuses to let go. Mom, calmly, asks if you ate. Family is a planet with its own gravity.

choices.text: Tell Mom everything about Nolan
choices.consequence: Don't carry her in the dark.

choices.text: Eat the pie and say nothing
choices.consequence: Some weeks, dinner is the win.

nodes.text: Nolan finally drops you an encrypted note: he's hiding from Viltrum on a backwater world. He needs you to come retrieve a device he stole from Lucan. The device might save Earth. It might also be a test. With Nolan, it's always both.

choices.text: Go fetch the device
choices.consequence: Risk one trip for a planet.

choices.text: Refuse and force him to come to you

nodes.text: A villain you haven't seen in two seasons rampages through midtown for reasons he refuses to explain. He is, frankly, having a bad mental-health day. You can tell.

choices.text: Talk him down
Take him to Dr. Singh — the doctor, not the experiment

nodes.text: Allen the Alien drops in for tacos and bad news. The Coalition of Planets is, again, asking Earth to take a side. Eve, beside you, is too tired to roll her eyes. Allen has, somehow, brought salsa.

choices.text: Say yes to the Coalition formally
choices.consequence: Pick a side before sides pick you.

choices.text: Hold out for a better deal

nodes.text: Eve sits down on the curb and admits, quietly, that she doesn't know if she wants to be Atom Eve anymore. The world is loud, the work doesn't end, and her energy doesn't recharge as fast as it used to.

choices.text: Tell her you'll take her shift
Tell her she should rest as long as she needs

nodes.text: Lucan comes back with a fleet. He does not, in the conventional sense, ask permission. He addresses the planet through every TV and phone at once and announces a 'transition.' Cecil curses fluently for thirty seconds.

choices.text: Take the fight to him in orbit
choices.consequence: Where his power is loudest, his ego is loudest too.

choices.text: Trap him on the ground with friends

nodes.text: Late at night you write, in a notebook nobody else will read, a list of who you owe an apology to, an explanation to, a sandwich to. The list is long. You go to bed planning to start at the top in the morning.

choices.text: Start with Eve in the morning
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Love first.

choices.text: Start with Amber in the morning

nodes.text: A skyscraper folds slowly under your back. Lucan smiles even as you punch him. He does not, you realize, want to win this fight. He wants to teach you what 'losing' costs.

choices.text: Refuse to play that lesson
Take the hit so he overextends

nodes.text: You and Robot and Eve and three reformed-ish villains pin Lucan in a containment field of Robot's design while Cecil's people negotiate. Nobody dies today. It is, almost, anticlimactic. It is, almost, a miracle.

choices.text: Bask in the quiet for a beat
Pivot immediately to the next problem
choices.consequence: There is always a next problem.

nodes.text: Mid-fight or mid-quiet, depending, your father lands. He is older. He is, apparently, on your side this time. He doesn't apologize. He never does. He helps, and that, this time, is enough.

choices.text: Let him stay for dinner with Mom
Tell him to go after the fight

nodes.text: Months later, somehow, you graduate college. Your mom cries. Eve is in the audience. Cecil is in the audience and pretending he isn't. Your name is read off a list. The list does not say Invincible.

choices.text: Take the photo as Mark
choices.consequence: Be a person for a day.

choices.text: Skip the photo and patrol

nodes.text: Nolan, terribly, attends Sunday dinner. Your sister stares. Mom is courteous. You learn that 'family' is a verb you do under fluorescents with too many plates. It is messy. It is yours. You like it.
You tell Nolan he can help the world and stay out of your house. He nods, almost proud. You sleep, for the first time in weeks, without dreaming of him. Some boundaries are kindnesses to yourself.
You become someone the news doesn't always know about. You take Eve to brunch on Saturdays. You teach your sister to ride a bike. You still save the world. You also live in it.

You patrol, you train, you keep watch. It is who you are. It costs you some birthdays. You are okay with that, mostly. Eve is, mostly, okay with that. 'Mostly' is, in this line of work, a long marriage.
